body.statement: For every \(p\ge2\), the one-root star construction contains a nonempty strict-inequality parameter region on which the pairwise rank matrix \(R\) is invariant under swapping the baseline with the root-intervention vertex. Consequently, no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).
body.justification: The obstruction shows that the correction needs entrywise support and marginal information, rather than a different scalar aggregation of the same ranks.
body.gap: Squires et al. use one rank score, but the literature does not establish an open-family impossibility for the entire class of equivariant rank-only selectors.
body.consumer: Method designers can rule out every rank-only baseline heuristic and focus on information-preserving summaries.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\ge2\) and a member of the one-root star family in
\(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\).  Put
\[
 d=\tau_1^{-1}-\omega_1^{-1}\neq0.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:surgery-identity}\), the root precision difference is
\[
 \Delta_1=d e_1e_1^{\top},
\]
and for each leaf \(j\ge2\), on coordinates \(\{1,j\}\),
\[
 \Delta_j=
 \begin{pmatrix}
 -b_j^2/\omega_j&b_j/\omega_j\\
 b_j/\omega_j&\tau_j^{-1}-\omega_j^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.                                                    \tag{21}
\]
All other rows and columns of \(\Delta_j\) vanish.  Its determinant is
\[
 \det(\Delta_j|_{\{1,j\}})
 =-\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}<0,
\]
so
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_0)=\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j)=2.      \tag{22}
\]
Likewise,
\[
 \det((\Delta_j-\Delta_1)|_{\{1,j\}})
 =\frac{d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}.                  \tag{23}
\]
The strict inequalities defining the family make (23) nonzero, and hence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_1)=2
 =\operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_0) \qquad(j\ge2).                       \tag{24}
\]
Also \(\operatorname{rank}(K_1-K_0)=1\).  Equations (22)--(24) show that
the transposition \(\sigma\) of component vertices \(0\) and \(1\) fixes
the entire rank matrix: entries between leaves are untouched, entries
from either \(0\) or \(1\) to a leaf are both \(2\), and their mutual
entry is \(1\).

The strict region is nonempty.  For example, take all
\(\omega_\ell=1\), take \(\tau_1=2\), take
\(\tau_j=1\) and \(b_j=1\) for all leaves.  Then
\(d=-1/2\) and every left side in the defining inequality equals
\(-1\).  Positivity, \(d\neq0\), \(b_j\neq0\), and all strict
inequalities persist on an open neighborhood.  Every point of this
neighborhood is in \(\mathcal M_p\): the root intervention changes
variance and every leaf has a nonzero parent even when
\(\tau_j=\omega_j\).

Let \(F\) be a component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector.
Equivariance means
\[
 F(P_\gamma R P_\gamma^{\top})=\gamma(F(R))
\]
for every component permutation \(\gamma\).  Since
\(P_\sigma R P_\sigma^{\top}=R\), it follows that
\[
 F(R)=\sigma(F(R)).
\]
No vertex in \(\{0,1\}\) is fixed by \(\sigma\); in particular
\(F(R)\neq0\), although component \(0\) is the true baseline.  Thus \(F\)
fails at every parameter point in this nonempty open family.  Since \(F\)
was arbitrary, no equivariant selector based only on \(R\) is universally
correct on \(\mathcal M_p\).
